architecture_decisions: - The authoritative Engineering Run resume transition remains owned by `EngineeringRunService.resume`. - The worker re-arm authorization decision uses an immutable scalar snapshot of the pre-resume run state. - Re-arm remains permitted only when the request began from `FAILED` and the successful resume result is no longer `FAILED`. - `WorkerRecoveryService.prepare_human_resume` and the existing `FAILED -> RECOVERING -> REASSIGNED` worker path remain unchanged. - Ordinary `/autonomous`, reconnect, page refresh and repeated acquisition still cannot restart a terminal worker by themselves. - The route correction creates no new model, source, repository, provider, deployment or REVIEW authority. - A deliberately identity-aliased route regression is required so this same-session ORM behavior cannot escape again.
work_items: - The `/resume` route captures the Engineering Run state as an immutable scalar before invoking `EngineeringRunService.resume`.
validations: - The `/resume` route captures the Engineering Run state as an immutable scalar before invoking `EngineeringRunService.resume`.
AC-01: validate protected requirement — The `/resume` route captures the Engineering Run state as an immutable scalar before invoking `EngineeringRunService.resume`.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — When the object returned by the pre-read is the same object mutated by `resume`, a request that entered from `FAILED` still invokes `prepare_human_resume` after a successful transition to an active stage.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — If the request begins from any state other than `FAILED`, the route does not invoke terminal-worker re-arm solely because the post-resume run is active.
AC-04: validate protected requirement — If the resume result remains `FAILED`, terminal-worker re-arm is not invoked even when the pre-resume scalar state was `FAILED`.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Eligible recovery still uses the existing v3.25 unleased `FAILED -> RECOVERING` preparation followed by the existing protected `RECOVERING -> REASSIGNED` lease-generation path.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Ordinary `/autonomous` calls, acquisition attempts, reconnects and page refreshes cannot re-arm a terminal worker without the explicit successful FAILED-run resume boundary.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — The correction does not rewrite or delete prior Engineering Run attempts/events, worker checkpoint evidence, source lineage, last-known-good lineage, current step or lease-generation history.
AC-08: validate protected requirement — Candidate bounds, validator-guided repair, hosted model ordering, source mutation, Git/provider delivery, deployment and REVIEW boundaries remain unchanged.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — A focused route regression deliberately mutates the same pre-read run object during `resume` and proves the recovery preparation still executes from the snapshotted scalar state.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Focused route/worker tests, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, client/browser/Skia, protected promotion and DSPy release gates pass. After exact-source production deployment, one explicit retry of the affected production run persists worker recovery evidence after `RUN_CONTROL / RESUMED` and progresses beyond the prior terminal-worker conflict.
risks: - The `/resume` route captures the Engineering Run state as an immutable scalar before invoking `EngineeringRunService.resume`.
